script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for January 10. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.

Here's a test: in your last conversation, were you really listening—or were you waiting for your turn to talk?  Most of us are thinking about what we'll say next while others are still speaking.  Today, we learn why that's a problem and how to fix it.

Immediately after a conversation, we remember only 50% of what was said. After 48 hours? Just 25%. And that's when we're trying. When we're planning our response while others speak, retention drops even further. Listening takes intention. We process speech 3 times faster than people can talk.  That cognitive surplus should help us think deeper about what we're hearing.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: Listening is not waiting.  It's not silence while you prepare to speak.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Full Presence - Listening Practice.

Here's your activity: In one conversation today, practice this: After the other person finishes speaking, count to 2 in your head before responding. Use that pause to make sure you understood, not to prepare your reply. This helps you develop the skill of listening without planning a response.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about the art of really listening can be applied to full presence - listening practice. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
